  "research_question": "How do different stimulation paradigms affect mouse navigation performance across five key metrics",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],

  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham condition shows poorest performance across all metrics: lowest success rate (0.273), highest time-to-target (4.682), lowest path efficiency (0.308), lowest average speed (10.737), and lowest angular dispersion (0.236)",
    "Bright Visual Only and Combined paradigms show best overall performance with similar metrics: success rates ~0.78, time-to-target ~2.6, path efficiency ~0.50, average speed ~12.7, and angular dispersion ~0.39",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only show intermediate performance between Sham and the top performers: success rates ~0.67-0.69, time-to-target ~3.0-3.1, path efficiency ~0.43, average speed ~12.0, and angular dispersion ~0.34-0.35"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sham vs Bright Visual Only: 1.8x difference in success rate (0.273 vs 0.785)",

    "Sham vs Bright Visual Only: 63% difference in path efficiency (0.308 vs 0.504)",
    "Sham vs Combined: 19.5% difference in average speed (10.737 vs 12.833)",
    "Sham vs Bright Visual Only: 64% difference in angular dispersion (0.236 vs 0.387)"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Both visual stimulation paradigms (Bright Visual Only and Combined) significantly improve navigation performance compared to no stimulation (Sham), with Bright Visual Only performing nearly as well as Combined stimulation.   ],

}
